title: FMGE PSM Day 1 Section 2
subject: Community Medicine
description: An 18-question PSM section from the reviewed Day 1 notes.

questions.stem: Which mosquito is the principal vector of rural malaria in India?
questions.explanation: Anopheles culicifacies is the principal rural malaria vector in India.

questions.stem: Which mosquito is the principal vector of urban malaria in India?
questions.explanation: Anopheles stephensi is the principal urban malaria vector in India.

questions.stem: Ticks of which genus transmit Kyasanur Forest disease?
questions.explanation: Kyasanur Forest disease is transmitted by Haemaphysalis ticks.

questions.stem: The neonatal period extends through approximately how many days after birth?
questions.explanation: The neonatal period comprises the first four weeks of life.

questions.stem: Disease-free exposed and unexposed groups are followed forward. Which capability is an advantage of this design?
options: Studying very rare diseases with small samples
Assessing several prior exposures for one disease
Assessing several outcomes after one exposure
questions.explanation: A cohort can assess multiple outcomes after a defined exposure.
questions.answer_label: Assessing several outcomes after one exposure
questions.answer: Assessing several outcomes after one exposure

questions.stem: Which study design can investigate several previous risk factors for one disease?
questions.explanation: Case-control studies can examine several prior exposures for one disease.

questions.stem: The Framingham Heart Study is a classic example of which study design?
questions.explanation: The Framingham Heart Study is a cohort investigation.

questions.stem: Compared with following exposure-defined groups forward, investigating prior exposures in disease-defined groups is generally:
questions.explanation: Case-control studies are generally quicker and less expensive than prospective cohorts.

questions.stem: In a single-blind trial, who is ordinarily unaware of the treatment allocation?
questions.explanation: In the conventional participant-blinded single-blind trial, the participant is unaware of allocation.
An open-label study keeps participants and investigators aware of treatment allocation.

questions.stem: Microdosing is associated with which phase of drug development?
questions.explanation: Phase 0 is associated with exploratory microdosing.

questions.stem: The principal objective of a Phase II clinical trial is assessment of:
questions.explanation: Phase II assesses therapeutic efficacy in patients.

questions.stem: Large comparative trials of a new drug against an existing treatment are generally conducted in:
questions.explanation: Phase III provides comparative assessment before marketing.

questions.stem: Which cases form the numerator of disease prevalence?
options: Deaths from the disease during follow-up
Recovered cases from the previous year
New cases arising during follow-up only
All current cases, both new and pre-existing
questions.explanation: Prevalence counts all current cases, including new and pre-existing cases.
questions.answer_label: All current cases, both new and pre-existing
questions.answer: All current cases, both new and pre-existing

questions.stem: Where is the headquarters of the International Labour Organization?
questions.explanation: The International Labour Organization is headquartered in Geneva.

questions.stem: Where is the headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization?
questions.explanation: The Food and Agriculture Organization is headquartered in Rome.

questions.stem: Which under-five mortality level, per 1,000 live births, is used as the reduction threshold in SDG target 3.2?
questions.explanation: The under-five mortality reduction threshold in SDG target 3.2 is 25 deaths per 1,000 live births.

questions.stem: Which neonatal mortality level, per 1,000 live births, is used as the reduction threshold in SDG target 3.2?
questions.explanation: The neonatal mortality reduction threshold in SDG target 3.2 is 12 deaths per 1,000 live births.
